Cinematic 21:9 anamorphic footage, 10 seconds, photorealistic, shot on 35mm with fine film grain. This clip continues exactly from the provided first frame for its first second, then it is EDITED TO THE BEAT: a HARD CUT to a new shot every two hammer hits, never three hits on the same shot, no dissolves, no morphing. Within each shot the camera is locked off or moves slowly in one direction.

The world is total darkness. Nothing is visible unless a sound touches it: every sound emits light that travels across surfaces like a wave, reveals only what it passes over, then fades back to pure black. The color is the sound. EVERYTHING IN THIS CLIP IS BORN FROM ONE SOUND: the metallic "tac" of the skull settling, which at the start of the clip is still hanging at its jaw as a short thread of white liquid light. That thread leaves the skull as a single simple ribbon of white light and starts to BOUNCE through the hall like an echo: it hits a pillar - TAC - and does not break: it gathers on the far side of the pillar, leaving only a thin cushion of light where it touched, and springs off to the next surface - a chain, the rubble, the water, a loudspeaker cone - TAC, TAC - every impact one metallic hit of sound and one burst of light where it lands. The bounces come faster and heavier, lock into a rhythm, and as the rhythm becomes a huge hammer-on-anvil beat the light turns from white to amber and orange: the hammer is amber.

THE WAVES ARE THE PROTAGONISTS, and they are the waves of reference image 3, which shows their five phases from left to right. BIRTH: at the centre of a loudspeaker cone glowing dust materialises, swirls and thickens into luminous smoke, then into liquid light. PROPAGATION: a single ribbon of light leaves the speaker and splits into several thin filaments, shifting slightly in colour as it travels through the air. INTENSIFICATION: the ribbons brighten from inside, thicker and more numerous, with electric filaments running along them. BOUNCE: when a wave hits a wall, a pillar, the water or the skull it does not break: it gathers on the far side of the object, leaving only a thin cushion of light where it touched, and travels on. ELECTRIC IMPACT: where a wave lands on the skull it turns electric: a web of tiny arcs of light hovers just above the black metal like static electricity, without touching it - the metal stays whole and smooth, no cracks, no glowing seams - this is what irritates it. Across the clip the waves grow through these phases in order: birth and propagation first, intensification in the middle, bounces everywhere, the electric web on the skull at the end. Once the beat has started the two loudspeaker stacks, struck by the bouncing light, pump with it and give birth to new waves on every hit; so the waves are irregular, never clean rings: they come off the speakers, the pillars, the chains, the rubble and the skull itself, cross each other on the black water and reach the skull from every side at once; where they overlap on the water they draw cymatic standing-wave patterns. Reflective surfaces - the black water, the polished black metal - amplify them; dull stone swallows them.

The place is the one in reference image 2: a ruined gothic hall at night - pointed arches and dark pillars, one wall collapsed into a pile of black rubble, a thin shaft of cold moonlight from a broken window high up, hanging chains, a shallow pool of black water on the floor with black metal remains lying in it, and two big loudspeaker stacks, one on the left and one on the right. Keep this place identical in every shot.

The subject is a skull of jet-black riveted metal, the skull of reference image 1: a complete skull with its lower jaw, glossy like oiled black iron, curved plates joined by rows of small dome-head rivets, heavy scowling brow, deep-set eye sockets, and a small red rectangular badge stuck on it with the word "CENSORED" printed in white capital letters. It stands upright on its chin in the black water in the middle of the hall and never leaves its place. In this clip the waves that keep hitting the skull IRRITATE it: shot after shot its expression hardens, in a crescendo - calm, then suspicious (brow lowering), then annoyed (brow pressing down, teeth grinding), then furious at the last hit. Nothing glows by itself: the skull and the hall are only ever seen as hard-edged amber reflections sliding over black metal, black water and wet stone, catching on the rivet heads.

nodes.title: Composer III Delirium
widgets_values:
Cinematic 21:9 anamorphic footage, 11 seconds, photorealistic, shot on 35mm with heavy film grain. This clip starts exactly from the provided first frame: a frontal medium close-up of the skull in near-total darkness, its jaw ALREADY dropped wide open, the only light a small magenta glow igniting inside its open mouth - no amber, no ribbons yet. Shots change with HARD CUTS, no dissolves, no morphing; within a shot the camera shakes with the sound.

The world is total darkness. Nothing is visible unless a sound touches it: every sound emits light that travels across surfaces like a wave, reveals only what it passes over, then fades back to pure black. The color is the sound. In this clip the sound is the skull's own VOICE: a scream, and the voice is magenta and ultraviolet, with pure white on the loudest peaks. No amber, no cyan.

THE WAVES ARE THE PROTAGONISTS, the waves of reference image 3. Left panel, SPECTRUM: when the skull screams, many waves at once, each a different colour - magenta, violet, ultraviolet, white - pour out of its open mouth as ribbons of liquid light and fly through the hall. Middle panel, ENTRY: when a wave comes back and reaches an opening - an eye socket, the mouth - its layers are drawn into the opening; as they enter they turn electric and throw small sparks on the metal around it. Right panel: two ribbons drifting into phase with each other. It is the SCREAM, not any music, that makes the world vibrate: in this clip the waves are VIOLENT and unruly - they slam into every surface, bounce off pillars, chains, rubble and the two loudspeaker stacks, cross each other everywhere, and where they hit they DEFORM what they touch: the black water heaves and buckles, the rubble jumps, the chains whip, and the skull's own black plates ripple and warp for an instant and snap back; the image itself stutters and tears like a broken video signal on the loudest peaks. When a wave hits the skull it does not break: it gathers on the far side, leaving a thin cushion of light where it touched.

The place is the one in reference image 2: a ruined gothic hall at night - pointed arches and dark pillars, a collapsed wall of black rubble, a thin shaft of moonlight from a broken window high up, hanging chains, a shallow pool of black water with black metal remains lying in it, two loudspeaker stacks left and right. The subject is the skull of reference image 1: jet-black riveted metal, a complete skull with its lower jaw, glossy like oiled black iron, curved plates joined by rows of small dome-head rivets, heavy scowling brow, deep-set eye sockets, a small red rectangular badge with the word "CENSORED" in white capital letters; it stands upright on its chin in the black water in the middle of the hall and never leaves its place; its jaw can open and close, its brow can move, nothing else about it changes. The metal stays whole: no cracks, no glowing seams. Nothing glows by itself except the light of the voice.

The clip ends in TOTAL BLACK and TOTAL SILENCE with a HARD CUT: the skull INHALES and the last waves are sucked into the eye sockets and the mouth together, and everything is gone - one frame lit, the very next frame fully black; no fade to black, no dimming.

Too much sound breaks the picture: on the heaviest hits the frame tears horizontally for a frame and snaps back.

The place is the ruined gothic hall of reference image 2: a wide hexagonal stone hall in ruins, thick broken pillars, rubble, hanging rusted chains, a shallow black pool of still water in the middle, two loudspeaker stacks.

The skull is the skull of reference image 1: jet-black riveted metal, a complete skull with its lower jaw, glossy like oiled black iron, curved plates joined by rows of small dome-head rivets, heavy scowling brow, a small red rectangular badge with the word "CENSORED" in white capital letters. Its eyes are ALIGHT: a thin bright cyan neon rim around each socket and a living mass of churning red embers inside. It is the head of THE LEADER of reference image 3: a man-shaped frame of the same black riveted iron plates (never bone, never chrome), wearing a dark-red studded leather biker vest with silver studs and zips, black leather pants, heavy black boots, and chains hanging from his neck and belt; the black skull with burning eyes is his head. Under the flashes the black iron stays black: a flash only draws colored highlights along the rivet rows, the plate edges, the studs and the wet surfaces.

THE BAND, four more figures built like the Leader - man-shaped frames of black riveted iron plates, never bone, never chrome - each with his own clothes: CHIODO of reference image 4 (black studded leather biker jacket, ripped jeans, chains), TOPPE of reference image 5 (denim jacket covered in patches, spiked hair), CAPPUCCIO of reference image 6 (black hoodie with the hood up over the skull), CANOTTA of reference image 7 (black tank top, bare iron arms, the most athletic). Every one of them has the same black skull for a head, eyes alight - cyan rim, red embers.

In this clip the band APPEARS, one figure per hit of the music, and every appearance is a SPECTACLE: nobody walks in from the side, nobody is there before his moment - each one materializes IN FRAME, out of the hall itself: out of a pillar, up through the floor, down from the darkness above, out of an empty hoodie on the ground. Each appearance is one hit, one flash of one color, one new angle. At the end all five headbang together in sync; the clip ends mid-motion on a hit.

HEADBANGING in this clip means the head whipping UP AND DOWN on the beat - chin slamming down to the chest and snapping back up, the whole upper body folding forward on every chug - NEVER side to side, never shaking or turning the head left and right.

widgets_values:
## RESONANCE — how to run

**Final workflow: 9 scenes, one Run.** Every *MM H3 Scene* has its seed fixed (`control_after_generate = fixed`), `previous_from = loop` and its own `handoff_frames` (22 = 0.92 s; the last scene, V-b2 Collapse, uses 5). *Loop Range*: `start_scene 0`, `scene_count 9`. Press **Run**: the loop renders scene 0 from its keyframe, then every scene from the tail of the previous one, video **and audio**; the *Handoff Tail* node at the end of the loop body cuts the tail the NEXT scene asks for.

**Output:** `output/MM_H3_Loop/scene_<i>_S_<seed>_*.mp4` (the `-audio.mp4` files carry the sound). To rebuild the film, concatenate them trimming the first `handoff_frames` of every clip after the first (they repeat the previous tail) — script and diary in the repo, `workflows/RESONANCE.md`.

**Needs** the MiniMax H3 int8 checkpoint + turbo LoRA, its text encoder and the two VAEs (video, audio) in the *Models* group, ~64 GB of system RAM (text encoder 25 GB + diffusion 19.5 GB) and 24 GB of VRAM: restart ComfyUI before a full run. About 10 min per 10 s scene on an RTX 3090.

**Re-render one scene only:** on its *MM H3 Scene* set `previous_from = file` and `resume_from_video` = the previous clip, then *Loop Range* `start_scene` = its index, `scene_count = 1`.

**Scenes:** 0 I-a Drops · 1 I-b Tac · 2 II Hammer · 3 III Delirium · 4 IV Silence · 5 V-a1 Awakening · 6 V-a2 Apparitions · 7 V-b1 Pogo · 8 V-b2 Collapse. **References:** the skull character sheet (ref 1), the Dirock hall (ref 2), the wave-phase storyboards, the band character sheets Leader / Chiodo / Toppe / Cappuccio / Canotta.

1 · SCENES — how to read this section
widgets_values:
## 1 · SCENES — one Composer + one Scene per act

**MM H3 Scene Prompt Time Composer** turns a storyboard into an H3 prompt with a time-code per beat: `intro` (world, camera, style — the part every beat shares), a table of **beats** (name · base duration on a 10 s reference · locked/scaled · text, each written as `SOUND: … IMAGE: …` so audio and picture are born together), `total_duration`, a global `sound` line and an `avoid` line. Locked beats keep their seconds, the others scale with the duration, the last unlocked one absorbs the remainder, so the `[0.0-1.0s]` tags always add up. Outputs: the prompt, a readable timing table, the duration and the real frame count (H3 only accepts 17k+5 frames at 24 fps).

**MM H3 Scene** packs the prompt with everything else the scene needs: `seed`; where its first frame comes from (`previous_scene` = the loop hands over the last frame of the previous clip; `first_frame` = a keyframe; `none`); an optional `last_frame` the clip must land on; up to 9 reference images, cited in the prompt as `<Picture n>`; `handoff_frames` (how much of the previous clip's tail is re-rendered at the join — 22 = 0.92 s; the final collapse uses 5); `previous_from` (`loop`, or `file` + a path, to resume from any clip).

**MM H3 Collect Scenes** lines them up in socket order: that list is the whole film. On the right: the keyframes and references the scenes plug in (character sheets, the hall, the wave-phase storyboards).

In RESONANCE only scene 0 starts from a still (the crooked skull in the pool = `last_frame` of I-a, wired as `first_keyframe` of *Loop Range*); every other scene continues from the clip before it, video and audio. Hover a widget for its tooltip; select a WextraX node and press **?** for the full help page.

## 2 · LOOP — which scene runs now

**MM H3 Loop Range** reads the scene list and decides the run: `start_scene` / `scene_count` (0/9 = the whole film in one Run; 3/1 = only scene 3, resuming from the clip its Scene node names). It outputs `run_count` for the For Loop and what the first scene of the run starts from: the keyframe, or the tail + audio of the clip on file.

`scene index = loop index + start_scene` is the absolute index used everywhere; every clip is written as `scene_<index>_S_<seed>`. The For Loop (ComfyUI-Easy-Use) carries three values from one iteration to the next: **value1** = last frame, **value2** = hand-off tail clip, **value3** = hand-off audio.

widgets_values:
## 3–4 · H3 chain and OUTPUT — the loop body

**MM H3 Scene Conditioning** is the whole conditioning in one node: for `scenes[scene_index]` it encodes the prompt, sizes the canvas from the keyframe (`megapixels`), places first/last frame, guide and references and — when `handoff` is on and the scene continues from the previous one — anchors the previous tail (video + audio) at frame 0, so motion and sound carry across the cut. Its outputs feed the standard MiniMax H3 sampling: RandomNoise (seed from the scene) → BasicGuider → SamplerCustomAdvanced → VAE decode (video, tiled) + VAE decode (audio) → VHS Video Combine writes `output/MM_H3_Loop/scene_<i>_S_<seed>_*.mp4` (the `-audio.mp4` has the sound).

**MM H3 Handoff Tail** closes the iteration: from the clip just rendered it cuts the tail the NEXT scene asks for (its `handoff_frames`) plus the matching audio, and the last frame — the three values the loop end carries to the next scene. After the loop: cache clear + VRAM free, the final last frame and the list of files written.

To rebuild the film from the clips, concatenate them trimming the first `handoff_frames` of every clip after the first (they repeat the previous tail) — script and diary in the repo (`workflows/RESONANCE.md`).
